==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ləʊn/|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/loʊn/|a=US}} * {{audio|en|en-us-loan.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|əʊn|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|lone}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*leykʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|lone}}, {{m|enm|lane}}, from {{der|en|non|lán}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*laihną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leykʷ-||to leave (over)}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|lán}}, {{cog|sv|lån}}, {{cog|da|lån}}, {{cog|de|Lehen||fief}}, {{cog|nl|leen||fief}}, {{cog|fy|lien}}, {{cog|frr|leen||fief; loan; office}}, {{cog|sco|lane}}, {{m|sco|lain}}, {{m|sco|len}}, {{cog|ang|lǣn}}. More at {{m|en|lend}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|law|banking|finance}} An act or instance of [[lend]]ing, an act or instance of [[grant]]ing something for [[temporary]] use. #: {{syn|en|loaning|lending}} #: {{ux|en|Because of the '''loan''' that John made to me, I was able to pay my tuition for the upcoming semester.}} # {{senseid|en|Q189539}}{{lb|en|law|banking|finance}} A sum of [[money]] or other [[property]] that a natural or legal person [[borrow]]s from another with the condition that it be returned or repaid over time or at a later date (sometimes with [[interest]]). #: {{syn|en|principal}} #: {{ux|en|All '''loans''' from the library, whether books or audio material, must be returned within two weeks.}} #: {{ux|en|He got a '''loan''' of five thousand pounds.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=2|passage=''That'' the young Mr. Churchills liked—but they did not like him coming round of an evening and drinking weak whisky-and-water while he held forth on railway debentures and corporation '''loans'''. Mr. Barrett, however, by fawning and flattery, seemed to be able to make not only Mrs. Churchill but everyone else do what he desired.}} # The contract and array of legal or ethical obligations surrounding a loan. #: {{ux|en|He made a payment on his '''loan'''.}} # The permission to [[borrow]] any item. #: {{ux|en|Thank you for the '''loan''' of your lawn mower.}} =====Hypernyms===== * ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|usually|_|ditransitive|US|dated|_|and|occasionally|proscribed|_|in|_|UK|informal}} To [[lend]] (something) to (someone). #* {{quote-book|en|date=June 1 mentioned, to my utter astonishment, the fact of his having '''loaned''' Neilson 81000 to buy my bill on Maryland; and stated that he could not proceed to make the payment until Neilson refunded the |passage=All the rest—six out of eleven, more than half—were '''loaned''' to him.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Joanne M. Flood|title=Wiley GAAP 2015: Interpretation and Application of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=dtKSBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA574&dq=%22loaned%22%7C%22loaning%22&hl=en&sa=X&ei=GAKMVa3QBIbM8gWLn4PoDQ&ved=0CIUDEOgBMEY#v=onepage&q=%22loaned%22%7C%22loaning%22&f=false|page=574 |passage=Upon maturity of the debt, the investment bank returns the '''loaned''' shares.
On the date of issuance, the entity should record the '''loaned''' shares at their fair value and recognize them as an issuance cost, with an offset to additional paid-in capital.}} =====Usage notes===== * This usage, once widespread in the UK, is now confined to the US (or perhaps parts thereof). The use of ''loan'' as a verb is occasionally disapproved of, especially when the object being lent is something other than money; as a consequence, {{m|en|lend}} is often preferred. =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|loanability|loanable|loaner|reloan}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to lend}} * Armenian: * Asturian: * Azerbaijani: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * German: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Khmer: * Occitan: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|ссужа́ть}}, {{t|ru|дава́ть взаймы́}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Telugu: * Thai: * Turkish: * Vietnamese: * Walloon: {{trans-bottom}} ====Further reading==== * {{pedia}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{bor|en|gd|lòn||marshy meadow}} (compare {{m|gd|lèana||wet meadow, marsh, meadow}}). ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|Scotland|Northern England}} An area of uncultivated ground near a village or farmhouse. #: ''the '''Loan''' of Turchloy'', ''the Black '''Loan''''' #* {{quote-book|en|year=1800|author=Alexander Pennecuik|title=Lintoun Green; Or, the Third Market-day of June, 1685: A Poem, in Nine Cantos|page=38 |text=[...] The herds upon the '''loan''', As if a sheep had fled, wi' speed, At Grumphy tykes hound on Wi' loud huzza!}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1856|origyear=1822?|author=Sir Walter Scott|title=Waverley Novels|page=315 |text=[...] meeting in the '''loan''' above the house his own great plough with the six oxen, which were the pride of his heart.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1871|author=Henry Scott Riddell|title=The Poetical Works of Henry Scott Riddell|page=26 |text=When the dews begin to fauld the flowers, and the gloaming shades draw on, When the star comes stealing through the sky, and the kye are in the '''loan''', He whistles{{nb...}}}} =====Related terms===== {{col|en|lonnen}} ====References==== * {{R:EDD}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=alno|Laon|lona|nola|Anlo|NOLA|Alon|Nola}}
